transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-01-10
Start time: 15:00 PST
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Martinez (Redwood AE), Derek Huang (Redwood SE), Amir Patel (Redwood CSM), Lena Ortiz (Head of Platform, BluePeak), Markus Voss (CTO, BluePeak), Priya Shah (SRE Lead, BluePeak), Anil Rao (Procurement, BluePeak)
Recording id: rf-20270110-0428

Auto-generated summary (optional):
- Renewal discussion for contract expiring March 2027, BluePeak evaluating committed Dedicated capacity + additional EU region for data residency.
- Customer wants throughput guarantees for peak trading hours and lower p95 latency for inference.
- Action items agreed: pricing send, benchmarks in eu-west, IP allowlist and acceptance window.

Transcript:
[00:00] Sofia: Hey everyone thanks for hopping on, uh quick roll call, I think we have everyone, correct?
[00:04] Lena: Yep, Lena here.
[00:06] Markus: Markus on my end.
[00:08] Priya: Priya here.
[00:10] Anil: And Anil from procurement.
[00:12] Derek: Derek from Redwood, SE.
[00:13] Amir: Amir on CSM.
[00:15] Sofia: Great. So main goal today is to walk through renewal options, talk expansion — specifically additional region and capacity upgrade — and nail next steps. I'll try to keep it tight.

[00:35] Markus: Quick context — our contract's up in end of March, right? We're looking at committed capacity for inference across US and EU, and we need to firm up numbers for finance. Also, we have new regs in EU so data residency matters.

[00:50] Sofia: Yep that's right, March 31st. So two levers: Dedicated reserved capacity and then the region add-on for eu-west-1. We can do a multi-year commit to reduce unit cost. Derek will cover perf and what to expect.

[01:10] Derek: Cool. On the performance side we recommended pushing to 2x the current Dedicated pool during US peak, and adding a dedicated pool in eu-west for the region residency. The tradeoff is cost vs cold-starts and cross-region routing. We can also enable prefix caching and optimized batching to reduce token cost while preserving p95 latency.

[01:40] Priya: Question — can we get SLA numbers for p95 in eu-west? We saw p99 numbers in the docs but need tighter p95 for trading windows.

[01:50] Derek: Yeah, for Dedicated we can commit to p95 targets in the SLA — typical is 150–200ms for short prompts on A100 setups, but that depends on model and sequence length. With quantized variants we hit lower cost but slight p95 regressions, so it's a trade-off.

[02:20] Lena: Are there differences if we use Hosted API + region pinning versus full Dedicated in eu-west?

[02:30] Derek: Hosted with region pinning can get you closer quickly but you don't get isolated capacity guarantees. Hosted is multi-tenant, so during peak you might see noisy neighbors. Dedicated gives you the reserved GPU pool, autoscale policies and burst capacity if you buy burst add-on. For strict latency and data residency I'd recommend Dedicated in eu-west.

[03:05] Markus: Cost side — finance will want committed discounts. What's the delta between 1-year and 3-year?

[03:12] Sofia: We'll send the pricing sheet but high level: 1-year committed gives about 18% discount vs on-demand; 3-year pushes to ~30% depending on absolute commit. Adding an extra region is a regional add-on, around 25% of a full pool cost if you want mirrored capacity, but we can tailor. I'll attach the proposal: https://redwood.ai/pricing/bluepeak-proposal-2027.pdf

[03:45] Anil: Can you include a line item for data egress and for cross-region replication? Procurement needs clarity on hidden fees.

[03:52] Sofia: Absolutely, we'll break out egress and cross-region costs.

[04:05] Derek: Also small note — if you plan to keep KV cache warm across regions, that increases the replication cost. We sometimes recommend async cache priming to reduce replication traffic.

[04:25] Priya: For security/compliance — we need SOC2 type II evidence, KMS integration for keys, and detailed audit logs. Are those included for Dedicated?

[04:35] Amir: Yes, Dedicated includes audit logs and can integrate with customer KMS (HSM or cloud KMS). We also have Private deployment options if you need full VPC private control plane, but that is a heavier lift and licensing model. We have a security deck I'll share.

[04:50] Lena: We're leaning away from full Private unless absolutely necessary. Main thing is EU residency and SSO / SAML + RBAC for teams.

[05:00] Derek: SSO SAML and RBAC are standard for enterprise. For retention you can set retention policy per workspace; let us know retention days for logs and model usage.

[05:20] Markus: For performance validation — can Redwood run a benchmark in eu-west with our corpus? We want to simulate our 100k qps spikes during open market.

[05:30] Derek: Yes we can. We'll run an end-to-end run using your test corpus. Prefer to use an A100-style machine; if you want latency guarantees we'll use Dedicated nodes matching your target hardware. We'll publish the run results and console traces. Link to last run for reference: https://redwood.ai/benchmarks/eu-west-1-run-2026-12-15 (note: older run).

[06:05] Lena: How long does a benchmark take?

[06:08] Derek: Typically 1–2 business days to set up, then a test window of a few hours. We'll need your allowlist and test window.

[06:20] Priya: On the note of telemetry — we need token-level cost breakdown and per-route dashboards to show business teams. Is that available in the Dedicated console?

[06:30] Amir: Yep console has per-route cost, latency histograms, token-level breakdowns. We can create a read-only dashboard for your finance folks.

[06:45] Anil: Is there any lock-in if we do a 3-year commit? Data portability, export of usage, etc.

[06:52] Sofia: No vendor lock-in for models, you can pin versions and export logs and usage. Commit is for capacity pricing only. We'll add explicit export clauses to the contract.

[07:10] Markus: Another question — do you support region-by-region rollouts? We may want to start US Dedicated and then add EU after a month. Can rollouts be staggered and is there pro-rated billing?

[07:20] Sofia: Yes staggered rollouts are common. Billing is pro-rated for the month you add the region. If you sign a commit covering both regions upfront, we can do staged activation while keeping the committed discounts.

[07:45] Lena: Let's talk about scale. Current usage is around 400M tokens/month, spiking to 2B during campaign windows. We're projecting 1–1.5B average next year. Finance wants a committed baseline and an overage model.

[08:05] Sofia: For forecasting that's helpful. We can propose a baseline for committed capacity and a predictable overage rate. Also, we can offer auto-burst credits if you want to cap overage cost.

[08:25] Derek: Re: model variants — if you can tolerate slight quality regression you can use quantized 4-bit variants in Dedicated which reduces cost but increases latency slightly. For critical trading prompts I'd keep full float. We can mix and match by route.

[08:55] Priya: Do you support per-route model pinning so sensitive routes stay on full float and others use quantized?

[09:00] Derek: Yes. You can configure per-route model settings and rollout policies, even fallback to hosted smaller models if Dedicated is saturated.

[09:20] Markus: On the security paperwork — we'll need SOC2 and ISO certification details and penetration test results. Also, we may want contractual language about subprocessor list.

[09:30] Amir: We'll share the security pack. I'll send SOC2 attestation, pen test summary, and current list of subprocessors.

[09:40] Anil: Procurement will also want termination for convenience and exit assistance pricing. Can you add an exit assistance line?

[09:46] Sofia: Yes we can add exit assistance (data export and runbooks) as a subscription add-on, we'll include pricing.

[10:05] Lena: Ok timeline — finance wants numbers by next Monday to align with Q1 budget. That is 2027-01-17. Could you get pricing and a benchmark plan by then?

[10:15] Sofia: We'll aim for pricing by 2027-01-12 and a benchmark start by 2027-01-14. Derek, can you confirm bench availability?

[10:22] Derek: I can confirm. I'll schedule bench for 2027-01-14 to 2027-01-15 in eu-west-1 but need BluePeak to provide test corpus and allowlist by 2027-01-13.

[10:35] Priya: One more thing — we have internal compliance asking about key management. If we bring our own KMS, do you store keys?

[10:40] Amir: We support customer-managed keys via cloud KMS or HSM, Redwood never stores plaintext key material.

[11:00] Lena: Great. On contract length — if we commit 3 years, is there a possibility to lock pricing for add-on regions?

[11:06] Sofia: We can price and reserve optional region add-ons at contract signing at a slightly reduced rate if you commit. We'll show scenarios in the pricing worksheet.

[11:25] Markus: Competitor checks — we've talked to Anthropic and Google Vertex. Anthropic's price-performance looked good for some use cases but they don't offer the same Dedicated isolation options. Vertex has deep integrations but GCP lock-in concerns.

[11:40] Sofia: Noted. We'll highlight differences in the proposal.

[11:55] Anil: Procurement asks for a single point of contact for contract questions. Who should that be?

[11:58] Sofia: That will be me. Please loop in Amir for post-signature onboarding.

[12:10] Derek: I'll also be the technical owner for the benchmark and can attend onboarding calls.

[12:30] Sofia: Cool. Recap of next steps: I'll send pricing worksheet by 1/12, Derek will schedule bench in eu-west and share run plan, BluePeak to share test corpus and allowlist. We'll also send SOC2 + security docs.

[12:55] Lena: Sounds good. Anything else?

[13:00] Priya: No, thanks.

[13:05] Sofia: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email.

[13:08] (meeting ends)

Notes: Transcript contains minor transcription errors and shorthand (Redwood Dedicate noted in one auto-generated section). References shared: pricing proposal link above, benchmark link above, security pack will be sent (internal link to be shared).
